title: Cybersecurity Daily Briefing
description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities, major incidents, and threat trends relevant to enterprise and federal networks.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 24–30. New: CISA on Oct. 29 added a GitLab CI/CD bug and a Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD VPN bug to the KEV catalog, both due Nov. 1. The php2shell catalog due date was Oct. 29, and that item was removed because the due date has passed. The Linux kernel bug that CISA says can be chained with php2shell remains due Oct. 31. No new public update on the DMDC personnel breach was found.

items.headline: CISA adds a GitLab code-execution bug and a Cisco firewall VPN bug, both due Nov. 1
items.summary: CISA said Oct. 29 it added CVE-2026-97229, a GitLab integer-overflow bug, and CVE-2026-76418, a Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD bug, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 1 for both, requires forensic triage for the GitLab bug, and does not require it for the Cisco bug. CISA says the GitLab flaw could let an unauthenticated user run arbitrary code on the server with a crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, and GitLab's Oct. 12 patch release fixes it in 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8. Cisco says CVE-2026-76418 is in the remote-access SSL VPN service when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group, that an unauthenticated remote attacker can reload the device, that there is no workaround, and that its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026.

items.headline: CISA adds a Linux kernel bug chained with php2shell, due Oct. 31, and a VMware ESX logging bug
items.summary: CISA said Oct. 28 it added CVE-2026-46300, a Linux kernel missing-initialization bug, and CVE-2026-41709, a Broadcom VMware ESX insufficient-logging bug, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The catalog sets a due date of Oct. 31 for the kernel bug, marks it for forensic triage, and says it can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root. CISA describes the kernel flaw as letting socket-buffer coalescing drop a shared-fragment marker so ESP input processing decrypts shared fragments in place and can modify page-cache-backed data. The ESX entry is due Nov. 11, does not require forensic triage, and says a malicious actor with admin access could perform certain operations without them being logged.

items.headline: CISA adds Brotli and an Adobe Commerce bug to the KEV catalog, due Nov. 10
items.summary: CISA said Oct. 27 it added CVE-2026-48356, an Adobe Commerce and Magento unrestricted file-upload bug, and CVE-2026-111497, a Google Brotli unchecked-return-value bug, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 10 for both and describes the Brotli flaw as letting a remote unauthenticated attacker corrupt decoder memory, disclose memory, cause a denial of service, or potentially run code with a crafted compressed stream. SecurityWeek reported Oct. 28 that the Brotli bug, also called Node2Shell, affects Brotli 1.0.3 through 1.2.0, that federal civilian agencies were told to address it by Nov. 10, and that Broadcom warned Oct. 27 that SDDC Manager in VMware Cloud Foundation is affected because it uses Node.js, with patches still pending. SecurityWeek also said two honeypot operators logged attempts, and that ELLIO called the exploit it analyzed broken.

items.headline: Federal News Network: the CMMC task force lists a 90-day path to restart Phase 2
items.summary: Federal News Network reported Oct. 27, in the second part of its CMMC investigation, that a Defense Department task-force summary of the July request for information sorts reform options into changes the CIO could make without rulemaking, harder changes that may need rulemaking, and ideas outside the CIO's authority. The outlet says the summary, which it obtained, lists a 90-day option to restart Phase 2 for a narrower population, more guidance for assessors through the Cyber AB and CAICO, and an expansion of plan-of-action eligibility to 270 days that would require rulemaking. It also says the department wrote that clearer controlled-unclassified-information marking has the greatest potential to shrink the population that must implement NIST 800-171, and that the department declined to comment. Katie Arrington, who previously performed the CIO's duties, told Federal News Network the audit process has to start in order to be refined.

items.headline: CISA publishes a 2030 strategy with 60-, 180- and 365-day milestones
items.summary: CISA said Oct. 26 it released CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail. Acting Director Nick Andersen called on critical-infrastructure owners, operators, vendors and technology manufacturers to act, and the release says the strategy is meant to identify, disrupt and eliminate adversarial access. CISA names three pillars: Defend, lead national cyber defense; Harden, prioritize national infrastructure security; and Prevail, mobilize national resilience. The release says CISA will begin reviewing core services within 60 days, provide an implementation plan within 180 days, and report progress within 365 days. It also says CISA will keep its role, delegated by Homeland Security, in starting and restoring National Security and Emergency Preparedness communications.

items.headline: Federal News Network: CMMC cost complaints in the RFI point at NIST 800-171, not the assessments
items.summary: Federal News Network reported Oct. 26 that the Defense Department reviewed 997 responses to its Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification request for information, 509 of them (51 percent) from the defense industrial base, and that an internal email lists NIST Special Publication 800-171 work, including Microsoft 365 GCC High, enclaves and inconsistent interpretation, as the top cost concern rather than CMMC itself. The outlet says the RFI put the average cost of CMMC, separate from NIST 800-171, at $47,000, and it quotes the department on that same average assessment cost, set against Kelly Loeffler's July statement that complying could cost as much as $600,000. Federal News Network says the review is past the 75 days Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies set in July, that the department declined to comment, and that as of September 2,433 companies had Level 2 third-party certifications.

items.headline: Cisco: eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys can be brute-forced, and firewalls are still under review
items.summary: Cisco's informational advisory, first published Oct. 23 and updated Oct. 24, says a researcher showed that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates can be brute-forced in seconds because of an error in an April 2025 key ceremony, and that anyone with those keys can issue fraudulent TLS certificates for any domain. Cisco says two of the eight are code-signing CAs, and that all eight were cross-signed by Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root in May 2025. Cisco PSIRT said it is not aware of malicious use. Secure Firewall Management Center has a remediation article, while Secure Firewall ASA, Threat Defense, and Identity Services Engine were still under investigation in the Oct. 24 update.
